name: commit
description: Record what is staged as a commit. Stage first with git/add: this never stages anything itself, and an empty index is refused rather than committed as nothing. Check what you are about to record with git/diff staged=true.

message.description: The commit message. A subject line, then a blank line, then the body. Written verbatim: lines beginning with # are kept, not treated as comments.

author.description: Who wrote the change, as "Name <email@example.com>". Records authorship only; the committer is still git's configured identity, which must exist either way. Omit unless you are committing work on someone else's behalf.

max_files.description: Maximum number of committed paths to list back. The output says so when it truncates.

output_schema.description: The short sha and subject on the first line, then a blank line, then the paths the commit touched, one per line. Nothing else: the sha is what a later step needs, and the paths are how a flow checks it recorded what it meant to.

exit_codes.0: success (the sha and what it recorded are on stdout)
exit_codes.2: invalid input (stdin was not a JSON object, message is missing, or author is not 'Name <email>')
exit_codes.4: not permitted (the git repository is above the workspace root)
exit_codes.5: no repository (the workspace is not a git repository, or git is not installed)
exit_codes.6: refused (nothing is staged, or a commit hook rejected it)
exit_codes.7: no identity (git has no user.name and user.email to record the commit under)
